title: Implement Google OIDC callback and token validation
summary: Completed Google OIDC callback handling with one-time PostgreSQL state consumption, exact non-retried PKCE code exchange, strict RS256/JWKS and issuer/audience/azp/time/nonce validation, bounded key caching and rotation, stable-subject account creation or explicit recent-session linking, verified-email collision policy, session issuance/rotation, safe redirects, redacted categorized audit failures, configuration and synchronized documentation.

tests.notes: 12 runs, 113 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skips on final advisory-lock implementation
12 checks passed; RuboCop 194 files, architecture and data checks clean, Brakeman 0 warnings, gem/importmap audits clean
120 prompts; catalog and state consistent before completion

decisions: Use strict application-owned RS256 verification with canonical JWT/JWK parsing; cache only validated public JWKS keys per web process for a bounded TTL; consume valid state before the non-retried code exchange; keep provider tokens transient; never merge accounts by email
risks: JWKS cache is intentionally per web process so a cold process fetches independently; an ambiguous or failed one-shot code exchange consumes the transaction and requires a fresh sign-in attempt
next_steps: Prompt 019 implements the distinct GitHub OAuth flow without importing OIDC semantics
